question: What is the tenure of the Central Board of Directors in Reserve Bank of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Four years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tenure of the Central Board of Directors of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is **four years**.
 
• The Central Board of Directors is the highest decision-making body of the RBI, responsible for the bank's overall supervision and direction.
 
• It is constituted as per the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The Central Board of Directors consists of the Governor, Deputy Governors, and other members appointed by the Government of India.
 
• The tenure of these members ensures continuity in decision-making and stability in the functioning of the RBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):** The RBI is India's central banking institution, established on **1 April 1935**, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• **Composition of the Central Board:** It includes the Governor, four Deputy Governors, and 10 non-official directors nominated by the government, along with other members as per the Act.
 
• **Functions of the Board:** The Central Board formulates policies for the regulation of the issuance of currency, management of foreign exchange, and ensuring monetary stability in the country.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The RBI operates under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
 
• **Importance of Tenure:** A four-year tenure provides the board members sufficient time to implement policies effectively, ensuring long-term economic and financial stability.
